items.title: Theorem 7.A: an unconditional objective-value dichotomy
items.note: Theorem 7.A (lines 47-56, with disp/002): for F : Vec n → ℝ (finite = real-valued) with ConvexOn ℝ univ F and Homogeneous.PositiveDegreeOne F (F(tx) = tF(x), t ≥ 0), every R : AdmissibleBFGSRun n F has F(x_k) → 0 or F(x_k) → -∞ (Tendsto … atBot). Dimension n arbitrary (n = 0 vacuous, prose/025). The admissible-run structure (01_I convention: nonzero gradients at differentiable accepted points, H₀ ≻ 0, α_k > 0, fixed 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1, Armijo, weak Wolfe) records convexity, so _hF is unused. No bound on iterates, steps, lengths or matrices and no finite gradient alphabet is assumed (prose/006). The library proves it as AdmissibleBFGSRun.homogeneous_value_dichotomy (target homogeneousDichotomy). Non-vacuous: Global.absRun on |x| (example at the end).

items.title: Theorem 7.B: a many-piece extension of the common-tilt geometry
items.note: Theorem 7.B (lines 72-89, with disp/003, disp/004): for F = max_i a_iᵀx (hF_def): (i) every admissible run R and G = {v | ∃ᶠ k in atTop, R.g k = v} (gradients occurring infinitely often): a finite limit of F(x_k) gives 0 ∈ affineSpan ℝ G; (ii) if 0 ∉ affineSpan ℝ (Set.range a), every admissible run has F(x_k) → -∞. No bounded-displacement hypothesis (prose/010). Proof: lines 405-438 (Lemma 7.3 and prose/041). Non-vacuity: (i) is witnessed by Global.absRun on |x| = max(x,-x) (values → 0). For (ii) no admissible run is exhibited, and on many of its objectives none exists, so (ii) is vacuous there: if the slopes lie on one affine line missing 0 (any dimension), F is linear or a linear image of the two-piece model |u|+t, and no admissible run exists (maxLinear_line_no_run, via linear_objective_no_run and TwoPieceBudget.no_infinite_independent_two_piece); this covers every objective of (ii) in dimension ≤ 2 (maxLinear_affine_free_no_run: in dimension 1 all slopes coincide, in dimension 2 they lie on a line missing 0). Whether an admissible run exists for an objective of (ii) whose slopes do not lie on one line (at least three slopes, dimension ≥ 3) is not known. The text does not claim that such a run exists (its run statements are conditional, and it disclaims finite termination: prose/012, prose/045, where the open question is stated for the common-tilt family). (ii) is stated as printed.

"A useful arbitrary-many-piece family is f(u,t) = t + max_{1≤i≤m} b_iᵀu." Points of ℝ^{n+1} are (u,t) = Fin.snoc u t (t last, as in the TeX). tilt_family: if F(u,t) is the greatest of t + b_iᵀu for all u, t (hypothesis hF_def), then F is the finite max-linear objective (disp/001) with the m slopes (b_i,1), for every m and n. "Useful" is not a claim. The library's family Homogeneous.commonTilt puts t first.

items.anchor: A positively homogeneous function bounded below cannot take a negative
items.note: For positively homogeneous F (no convexity for the first claims): F(x) < 0 gives F(tx) → -∞ as t → ∞ ("otherwise f(tx) = tf(x) → -∞"); if F is bounded below then F ≥ 0, IsLeast (Set.range F) 0 and F(0) = 0 ("minimum value zero, attained at the origin"); every admissible run (whose structure includes convexity) has F(x_k) → 0.

items.anchor: If its sublevels are bounded, then \(f(x)>0\) for \(x\ne0\).
items.note: For finite convex positively homogeneous F with all sublevels bounded: F(x) > 0 for x ≠ 0; ∃ μ > 0, F(x) ≥ μ‖x‖ (Euclidean; in dimension 0 trivially); F(x_k) → 0 forces x_k → 0 for every sequence; every admissible run has x_k → 0.

items.anchor: The new theorem proves
items.note: F(x_k) → -∞ excludes a finite limit ("cannot stagnate on any finite value") for every infinite run on the family. As for prose/011: vacuous when the b_i lie on one line (tilt_collinear_no_run), open otherwise (prose/045).

items.anchor: proves the stronger finite-termination conclusion
items.note: A literature result, proved in the library (TwoPieceTerminationTarget) for the two-piece model F(u,t) = |u| + t and every 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1: with states (x, H ≻ 0, g = ∇F(x)) and steps = accepted Armijo–weak-Wolfe full-BFGS steps, (a) there is no infinite sequence of states joined by steps (and the reversed step relation is well founded), so every run of accepted steps is finite; (b) every state with no accepted step exposes unboundedness along its search direction -Hg (F(x - tHg) → -∞ as t → ∞, TwoPieceBudget.terminal_direction_unbounded); (c) from every state finitely many steps reach such a state. (a) and (b) give the text's claim: every run reaches, after finitely many iterations, a search direction exposing unboundedness. The Lean statement covers every Armijo–weak-Wolfe step choice, which includes the formulation of Xie–Wächter; the attribution itself is not checked.

items.anchor: \textbf{not} establish finite termination for the general many-piece
items.note: Open question, stated without proof: the text says that its argument does not establish finite termination for the general many-piece family f(u,t) = t + max_i b_iᵀu. Finite termination of every run on a member implies that no infinite admissible run exists on it; TiltNoInfiniteRunQuestion states this part (for all n, m, b: IsEmpty (AdmissibleBFGSRun (n + 1) F)). Proved here: it holds when the b_i lie on one line (tilt_collinear_no_run), in particular with at most two distinct b_i in every dimension (tilt_two_values_no_run, tilt_two_pieces_no_run) and for every member in ℝ² (tilt_plane_no_run); the same reduction (maxLinear_line_no_run: F is linear, linear_objective_no_run, or a linear image of |u|+t, TwoPieceBudget.no_infinite_independent_two_piece) shows that Theorem 7.B (ii) has no admissible run in dimension ≤ 2 (maxLinear_affine_free_no_run). Not known: b_i not on one line (at least three pieces, ambient dimension ≥ 3). Where the Prop holds, the run statements on the family (prose/011, disp/027, prose/043, prose/046) are vacuous. Earlier classified NON_CLAIM (scope remark); OPEN gives the question a precise Lean form.

items.note: Every infinite admissible run on the many-piece family has F(x_k) → -∞. As for prose/011: vacuous when the b_i lie on one line (tilt_collinear_no_run), open otherwise (prose/045).

items.note: UᵀH_KU ≻ 0, and for every z exactly one w ∈ H_KS (w = H_KUz') has Uᵀw = z.

items.anchor: In particular, convergence of the projected iterates implies convergence
items.note: If x̂_k → z_* then x_k → x_K + L_K(z_* - x̂_K).

items.anchor: The projected Hessian is \((U^\top H_kU)^{-1}\), not \(U^\top B_kU\).
items.note: (i) For k ≥ K the matrices (UᵀH_kU)⁻¹ = Ĥ_k⁻¹ follow the Hessian form (7.2.1) of the projected run with ĝ_k, ŷ_k, q_k, t_k (they are its Hessian approximations). "necessary for a valid reduction" is read as (ii).

items.anchor: In two dimensions, if \(g_k\) and \(g_{k+1}\) are linearly independent,
items.note: Standing assumptions of Section 7.7.2 in the plane: F = max_i a_iᵀx on ℝ², admissible run, f_k → 0. (i) for an independent transition the two pairings determine x_{k+1} (any z with the same two pairings equals x_{k+1}); (ii) one constant C with ‖z‖ ≤ C(|g_kᵀz| + |g_{k+1}ᵀz|) for all independent transitions and all z ("inverse norms uniformly bounded"; sup norm of Vec 2); (iii) endpoints x_{j+1} of independent transitions → 0 (for every ε, eventually ‖x_{j+1}‖ < ε along independent transitions), with no boundedness hypothesis. Linear independence is LinearIndependent ℝ ![u, v] (= pairDet ≠ 0 in the plane, linearIndependent_pair_iff).

items.anchor: An unchanged nonzero gradient cannot satisfy weak Wolfe on a strict
items.note: If gᵀs < 0 (strict descent) and c₂ < 1, then gᵀs ≥ c₂gᵀs fails; hence g_{k+1} ≠ g_k along every admissible run.

items.anchor: Distinct gradients that are positive multiples of one
items.note: For F = max_i a_iᵀx: along an admissible run, g_k = cg_j with c > 0 at iterates of positive value forces g_k = g_j; and if a_{i'} = ca_i with c > 1, a_i is active (F(x) = a_iᵀx) at no point with F(x) > 0 ("only the largest multiple can attain a positive maximum").

items.note: For F = max_i a_iᵀx (any dimension) and an admissible run with F(x_k) > 0 for all k: if g_k, g_{k+1} are linearly dependent then g_{k+1} = -κg_k with κ > 0. The library's planar form uses pairDet.

items.anchor: One source of noncompactness is a subspace of directions on which the
items.note: (i) If F is constant along a nonzero subspace V (F(x+v) = F(x) for v ∈ V), every nonempty sublevel is unbounded (noncompact). (ii) A finite max-linear objective is constant along the directions w with a_iᵀw = 0 for all i (the subspace S^⊥). The second sentence ("When this is the only source of noncompactness, the case is fully tractable in all dimensions") announces the theorem of disp/038, disp/039 and prose/065.
